## 4. From 400 primes to every prime

The experiment verified the factor patterns of $\Phi_{11}$ on 400 primes. (Its first run reported 400/400 *mismatches* — because one side was wrapped in an extra pair of brackets. The patterns themselves were perfect.) The pattern is now a theorem for every conductor:

**Factor-pattern theorem.** *For $p \nmid n$ and $t = \operatorname{ord}_n(p)$, $\Phi_n$ factors over $\mathbb{F}_p$ into $\varphi(n)/t$ irreducibles, each of degree $t$. This multiset is the cycle type of $x \mapsto px$ on $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$; in particular $p \equiv q \pmod n$ implies identical patterns.*

<details><summary><b>Proof sketch</b></summary>

A primitive $n$-th root of unity $\eta$ lies in $\mathbb{F}_{p^k}$ iff $n \mid p^k - 1$ iff $t \mid k$, so every root of $\Phi_n$ has degree $t$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$. On the group side, the cycles of $x \mapsto px$ are the cosets of $\langle p \rangle$, all of size $t$. Witnesses at $n=11$: $p=23$ gives $[1^{10}]$, $p=43$ gives $[2^5]$, $p=3$ gives $[5,5]$, $p=2$ gives $[10]$ (so $\Phi_{11}$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_2$).
</details>

The algorithm below computes the pattern the hard way — by distinct-degree factorization, with no reference to orders — and checks it against the orbit pattern.

{{algorithm:1}}

---

## 5. The tower and the extra bit

$\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{11})$ contains the real quintic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{11})^+ = \mathbb{Q}(2\cos(2\pi/11))$. Its type $T^+$ is $1$ on $\pm 1$ and $5$ elsewhere, so $H(T^+) = \log_2 5 - 8/5$, and the same remainder pins it. Going up the tower adds exactly one bit:
$$H(T \mid T^+) = 1 = \log_2 [\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{11}) : \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{11})^+].$$

<details><summary><b>The CRT explanation</b></summary>

$C_{10} \cong C_2 \times C_5$. The order of an element is the product of the orders of its components, the product is injective on $\{1,2\}\times\{1,5\}$, and the components are independent. Entropy is additive over independent readouts, so
$$H(T) = H_{C_2} + H_{C_5} = 1 + \left(\log_2 5 - \tfrac85\right).$$
</details>

Is the "one extra bit" special to $11$? The left panel below computes the gap $H(T) - H(T^+)$ for many primes and compares it with the *conjectured* law $2^{1 - v_2(\ell - 1)}$ — one bit when $\ell \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, half a bit when $\ell \equiv 5 \pmod 8$, and so on.

{{visualization:1}}

---

## 6. Semiprimes: multiplying fates

For $N = pq$ with independent uniform Frobenius classes, the remainder $N \bmod 11$ is the *product* of two remainders. The exact channel is
$$I\big(N \bmod 11;\ \{T(p),T(q)\}\big) = \log_2 5 + \tfrac{12}{25}\log_2 3 - \tfrac{47}{25} \approx 1.20271.$$

<details><summary><b>Where the $\log_2 3$ comes from</b></summary>

On the 100 equally likely pairs, each square class $N \in \{3,4,5,9\}$ is hit by exactly three ordered pairs of type $(5,5)$ and three of type $(10,10)$; each non-square class $N \in \{2,6,7,8\}$ by six pairs of type $\{5,10\}$. These cells of size $3$ and $6$ are the only source of $\log_2 3$. With $H(N) = \log_2 10$, $H(\text{pair}) = 2\log_2 5 - 93/50$ and $H(N, \text{pair}) = 2\log_2 5 + 51/50 - \frac{12}{25}\log_2 3$, the formula follows.
</details>

Three numbers were on the table: a measurement $1.2002$, an enumeration $1.1999$, and an earlier closed-form prediction $1.2027$. The exact law is within $3 \cdot 10^{-5}$ of $1.2027$ and strictly above the other two. In the lab below, draw finite samples and watch plug-in estimates scatter (with a visible bias) around the exact value. Then change the conductor $\ell$.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

The **attenuation** relative to a single prime is exact:
$$H(T) - I_{\text{semi}} = \tfrac{32}{25} - \tfrac{12}{25}\log_2 3 \approx 0.519 \text{ bits.}$$

---

## 7. The which-factor wall is not there

Does knowing *which* factor has which type — the ordered pair — tell you more about $N$? At degree ten: not one bit more. And the reason is structural.

<details><summary><b>Swap lemma and the wall theorem</b></summary>

*Swap lemma.* If an involution $\sigma$ fixes $Y$ and swaps the coordinates of a pair readout $O$, then $H(Y,O) = H(Y, \operatorname{sym}O) + P(O_1 \ne O_2)$: forgetting order costs exactly the off-diagonal probability, one bit per off-diagonal sample.

*Wall theorem.* If the residue satisfies $c(gh) = c(hg)$, apply the lemma with $\sigma(g,h) = (h,g)$, once with $Y = c(gh)$ and once with $Y$ constant; the two corrections cancel in the mutual information. This holds in every abelian group, and in every group whose residue is read through the abelianization, since $gh$ and $hg$ differ by the commutator $[g,h]$. It explains the zero walls previously computed for $A_4$ and $D_4$.
</details>

The demo checks the theorem on $(\mathbb{Z}/11)^\times$, on $S_3$ and $A_4$ read through their abelianizations — and shows a genuine nonzero wall once the hypotheses are broken.

    intro w hw
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := mem_product.mp hw
    exact hc w.2 h2 w.1 h1

    (fun q : G × G => c (q.1 * q.2)) (ordPair T) hX hO

    entropy_comp_of_injOn (φ := fun o => ((), o)) (fun _ _ _ _ h => by simpa using h)
  rw [hu1, hu2] at h2

theorem which_factor_wall_coset {S N : Finset G} {c : G → κ} (hd : IsDerivedFinset S N)

  have := hd.commutator_mem g hg h hh
  simpa [mul_inv_rev, mul_assoc] using this

/-- **Abelian case.**  For a finite abelian Galois group the wall vanishes for every residue
readout whatsoever. -/
theorem which_factor_wall_abelian {A : Type*} [CommGroup A] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]

    mutualInfo (univ ×ˢ univ) (fun q : A × A => c (q.1 * q.2)) (ordPair T) =
      mutualInfo (univ ×ˢ univ) (fun q : A × A => c (q.1 * q.2))

"""
Full pinning at degree ten: the cyclotomic field Q(zeta_11).

Numerical companion to the paper.  Everything is computed from scratch:

  1. The Frobenius type T(p) = ord_11(p) and its Chebotarev densities phi(d)/10.
  2. Exact type entropy H(T) = log2(5) - 3/5 and full pinning I(p mod 11; T) = H(T).
  3. The loss H(p mod 11 | T) = 8/5 bits, and per-class degeneracy H(T | p mod 11) = 0.
  4. An independent polynomial check: factor-degree patterns of Phi_11 over F_p
     (computed by distinct-degree factorisation, NOT from the order of p).
  5. The tower Q < Q(zeta_11)^+ < Q(zeta_11): H(T+) = log2(5) - 8/5, the tower bit,
     and the CRT split C10 = C2 x C5.
  6. The semiprime channel I(N mod 11; {T(p), T(q)}) = log2 5 + (12/25) log2 3 - 47/25,
     the vanishing which-factor wall, and the attenuation 32/25 - (12/25) log2 3.
  7. Certified enclosures of log2 5 and log2 3 from exact integer power comparisons.
  8. An empirical check of the densities on actual primes.

Only the Python standard library is used.

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections import Counter
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple, TypeVar

ELL: int = 11                     # conductor
UNITS: List[int] = list(range(1, ELL))   # (Z/11)^x, uniform Frobenius model
K = TypeVar("K", bound=Hashable)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- basic arithmetic
def mult_order(a: int, n: int) -> int:
    """Multiplicative order of a modulo n (gcd(a, n) = 1 assumed)."""
    a %= n
    k, x = 1, a
    while x != 1:
        x = (x * a) % n
        k += 1
    return k


def totient(n: int) -> int:
    return sum(1 for k in range(1, n + 1) if math.gcd(k, n) == 1)


def divisors(n: int) -> List[int]:
    return [d for d in range(1, n + 1) if n % d == 0]


def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i in range(n + 1) if sieve[i]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- information theory
def entropy(sample: Sequence[object], f: Callable[[object], K]) -> float:
    """Shannon entropy (bits) of the readout f on a uniform finite sample."""
    counts = Counter(f(w) for w in sample)
    n = len(sample)
    return -sum((c / n) * math.log2(c / n) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_info(sample: Sequence[object], f: Callable[[object], K],
                g: Callable[[object], K]) -> float:
    """I(f; g) = H(f) + H(g) - H(f, g)."""
    return (entropy(sample, f) + entropy(sample, g)
            - entropy(sample, lambda w: (f(w), g(w))))


def cond_entropy(sample: Sequence[object], f: Callable[[object], K],
                 g: Callable[[object], K]) -> float:
    """H(f | g) = H(f, g) - H(g)."""
    return entropy(sample, lambda w: (f(w), g(w))) - entropy(sample, g)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- polynomials over F_p
Poly = List[int]  # coefficient list, lowest degree first


def trim(a: Poly) -> Poly:
    while a and a[-1] == 0:
        a.pop()
    return a


def pmod(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a = a[:]
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    while len(a) >= len(b) and trim(a):
        if len(a) < len(b):
            break
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        s = len(a) - len(b)
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[s + i] = (a[s + i] - c * bi) % p
        trim(a)
    return a


def pmul(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    if not a or not b:
        return []
    r = [0] * (len(a) + len(b) - 1)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        if ai:
            for j, bj in enumerate(b):
                r[i + j] = (r[i + j] + ai * bj) % p
    return trim(r)


def pgcd(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a, b = trim(a[:]), trim(b[:])
    while b:
        a, b = b, pmod(a, b, p)
    inv = pow(a[-1], p - 2, p)
    return [(c * inv) % p for c in a]


def pdiv(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a = a[:]
    q = [0] * max(1, len(a) - len(b) + 1)
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    while len(trim(a)) >= len(b):
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        s = len(a) - len(b)
        q[s] = c
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[s + i] = (a[s + i] - c * bi) % p
    return trim(q)


def ppow_mod(base: Poly, e: int, m: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    result: Poly = [1]
    base = pmod(base, m, p)
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            result = pmod(pmul(result, base, p), m, p)
        base = pmod(pmul(base, base, p), m, p)
        e >>= 1
    return result


def factor_degree_pattern(f: Poly, p: int) -> List[int]:
    """Degrees of the irreducible factors of a squarefree monic f over F_p,
    by distinct-degree factorisation (independent of any group theory)."""
    pattern: List[int] = []
    f = f[:]
    h: Poly = [0, 1]          # x
    d = 0
    while len(f) > 1:
        d += 1
        if 2 * d > len(f) - 1:
            pattern.append(len(f) - 1)
            break
        h = ppow_mod(h, p, f, p)          # x^(p^d) mod f
        diff = h[:] + [0] * max(0, 2 - len(h))
        diff[1] = (diff[1] - 1) % p
        g = pgcd(f, trim(diff), p)
        k = len(g) - 1
        if k > 0:
            pattern += [d] * (k // d)
            f = pdiv(f, g, p)
            h = pmod(h, f, p)
    return sorted(pattern, reverse=True)


PHI11: Poly = [1] * 11  # 1 + x + ... + x^10


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the readouts
def T(g: int) -> int:
    """Frobenius type in Q(zeta_11): the order of g in (Z/11)^x."""
    return mult_order(g, ELL)


def T_plus(g: int) -> int:
    """Frobenius type in the real subfield: order of g in (Z/11)^x / {+-1} = ord(g^2)."""
    return mult_order(g * g, ELL)


def section(title: str) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 78 + f"\n{title}\n" + "=" * 78)


def main() -> None:
    log5, log3 = math.log2(5), math.log2(3)

    # 1. Chebotarev densities ---------------------------------------------------
    section("1. Frobenius types and Chebotarev densities in Q(zeta_11)")
    counts = Counter(T(g) for g in UNITS)
    for d in divisors(10):
        print(f"  ord = {d:2d}: residues {[g for g in UNITS if T(g) == d]!s:18s}"
              f" count {counts[d]}  phi(d) = {totient(d)}  density {Fraction(counts[d], 10)}")

    # 2. full pinning -------------------------------------------------------------
    section("2. Full pinning: I(p mod 11 ; T) = H(T) = log2 5 - 3/5")
    HT = entropy(UNITS, T)
    I = mutual_info(UNITS, lambda g: g, T)
    closed = -sum(totient(d) / 10 * math.log2(totient(d) / 10) for d in divisors(10))
    print(f"  H(T) (direct)            = {HT:.10f}")
    print(f"  cyclic closed form       = {closed:.10f}")

    print(f"  I(p mod 11 ; T)          = {I:.10f}")
    print(f"  H(T | p mod 11)          = {cond_entropy(UNITS, T, lambda g: g):.10f}  (per-class degenerate)")
    print(f"  H(p mod 11 | T)          = {cond_entropy(UNITS, lambda g: g, T):.10f}  (= 8/5)")
    print(f"  log2 10 - I              = {math.log2(10) - I:.10f}")

    ok = 0

    section("4. The tower Q < Q(zeta_11)^+ < Q(zeta_11)")
    HTp = entropy(UNITS, T_plus)

    S2, S5 = [1, 10], [g for g in UNITS if pow(g, 5, ELL) == 1]
    print(f"  CRT: H_C2 + H_C5         = {entropy(S2, T):.6f} + {entropy(S5, T):.6f}"
          f" = {entropy(S2, T) + entropy(S5, T):.10f}")

    # 5. semiprime channel ------------------------------------------------------
    section("5. Semiprime channel N = pq, independent uniform Frobenius classes")
    SP = [(g, h) for g in UNITS for h in UNITS]
    N = lambda w: (w[0] * w[1]) % ELL
    pair = lambda w: tuple(sorted((T(w[0]), T(w[1]))))
    ordered = lambda w: (T(w[0]), T(w[1]))
    Isemi = mutual_info(SP, N, pair)
    Iord = mutual_info(SP, N, ordered)
    print(f"  I(N mod 11 ; {{T(p),T(q)}}) = {Isemi:.10f}")
    print(f"  closed form              = {log5 + 12 / 25 * log3 - 47 / 25:.10f}")
    print(f"  I(N mod 11 ; (T(p),T(q))) = {Iord:.10f}")
    print(f"  which-factor wall        = {Iord - Isemi:.2e}")
    print(f"  attenuation H(T) - I     = {HT - Isemi:.10f}"
          f"   (32/25 - 12/25 log2 3 = {32 / 25 - 12 / 25 * log3:.10f})")
    print(f"  H(N mod 11) = {entropy(SP, N):.6f}, H(pair) = {entropy(SP, pair):.6f},"
          f" H(ordered) = {entropy(SP, ordered):.6f}")

    # 6. certified bounds -------------------------------------------------------
    section("6. Certified enclosures from exact integer powers")
    checks: List[Tuple[str, bool]] = [
        ("2^23219  < 5^10000   => log2 5 > 2.3219 ", 2 ** 23219 < 5 ** 10000),
        ("5^100000 < 2^232193  => log2 5 < 2.32193", 5 ** 100000 < 2 ** 232193),
        ("2^158496 < 3^100000  => log2 3 > 1.58496", 2 ** 158496 < 3 ** 100000),
        ("3^100000 < 2^158497  => log2 3 < 1.58497", 3 ** 100000 < 2 ** 158497),

    for s, b in checks:

    print(f"  I_semi in ({float(lo5 + Fraction(12, 25) * lo3 - Fraction(47, 25)):.6f},"

    section("7. Empirical densities on actual primes below 4,000,000")
